'''Andrew John Hoggard''' (born {{Birth based on age as of date|28|2003|07|04|noage=1}}) is a New Zealand [[Dairy farming|dairy farmer]] and politician.

Hoggard held leadership roles with the farmers' advocacy group [[Federated Farmers]] from 2014 to 2023, including as president for the final three years. He stepped down ahead of his election to the [[New Zealand House of Representatives]] as an [[ACT New Zealand]] list Member of Parliament.

He is [[Minister for Biosecurity]] and [[Minister for Food Safety]] in the [[Sixth National Government of New Zealand|Sixth National Government]].

==Early life==
Hoggard was born in 1974 or 1975,<ref name="ES 2003">{{cite news |title=Dairy farmer wary of sheep |date=4 July 2003 |first=Aaron |last=Smale |work=[[Manawatū Standard|Evening Standard]] |page=3}}</ref> the eldest son of Mike and Lynette Hoggard.<ref name="ES 2001">{{cite news |title=Region's farmers compete for title |date=6 March 2001 |work=[[Manawatū Standard|Evening Standard]] |page=9}}</ref> He was educated at [[Heretaunga College]] in [[Upper Hutt]],<ref name="Bulletin 2020">{{cite news |url=https://docplayer.net/docview/111/199421273 |title=Next luncheon guest speaker Andrew Hoggard |work=Bulletin |date=29 October 2020 |page=2 |publisher=Rotary Club of Wellington North |access-date=6 August 2023}}</ref> and went on to study at [[Massey University]], graduating with a Bachelor of Agricultural Economics degree in 1996.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://tamiro.massey.ac.nz/nodes/view/1392 |title=Graduation programme: 28–31 May 1996 |publisher=[[Massey University]] |year=1996 |page=47 |access-date=6 August 2023}}</ref>

==Farming career==
The Hoggards moved from Upper Hutt to a {{convert|186|ha|adj=on}} farm at [[Kiwitea]] in [[Manawatū District|Manawatū]] in 1998, with Andrew 50% [[sharemilking]] 440 [[Holstein Friesian]] cows on the farm owned by his parents.<ref name="ES 2001"/><ref name="DN 2001">{{cite news |title=Sponsors renew contest support |date=5 April 2001 |work=[[Taranaki Daily News|Daily News]] |page=20}}</ref>

In 2001, Hoggard competed in the Taranaki–Manawatū regional final of the [[New Zealand Young Farmers|Young Farmer of the Year]] contest.<ref name="DN 2001"/> The following year, he was again a regional finalist in the event, placing third,<ref>{{cite news |title=Taranaki farmer takes fourth place |last=Tacon | first=Terry |date=22 April 2002 |work=[[Taranaki Daily News|Daily News]] |page=4}}</ref> and in 2003 he won the Taranaki–Manawatū Young Farmer of the Year title.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hoggard heads for final |last=Tacon | first=Terry |date=31 March 2003 |work=[[Taranaki Daily News|Daily News]] |page=4}}</ref> He went on to compete in the 2003 national final,<ref name="ES 2003"/> but finished outside the top four.<ref>{{cite news |title=Southlander wins top farming prize |last=Morris | first=William |date=7 July 2003 |work=[[Southland Times]] |page=3}}</ref> In 2004, Hoggard finished third in the Taranaki–Manawatū regional final.<ref>{{cite news |title=Woodville sharemilker through to finals |last=Tacon | first=Terry |date=5 April 2004 |work=[[Taranaki Daily News|Daily News]] |page=4}}</ref>

Hoggard served as chair of the [[Federated Farmers]] Dairy Industry Group from 2014 to 2017, and was Federated Farmers vice-president from 2017 to 2020.<ref name="Bulletin 2020"/> On 26 June 2020, he succeeded [[Katie Milne]] as president of the organisation.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/rural/2020/06/big-gumboots-to-fill-federated-farmers-elect-new-president-and-board-members.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200627105536/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/rural/2020/06/big-gumboots-to-fill-federated-farmers-elect-new-president-and-board-members.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=27 June 2020 |title='Big gumboots to fill': Federated Farmers elect new president and board members |date=26 June 2020 |first=James |last=Fyfe |work=[[Newshub]] |access-date=6 August 2023}}</ref> He was elected to the board of the International Dairy Federation in November 2020.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/business/farming/123724767/manawat-dairy-farmer-andrew-hoggard-elected-to-international-dairy-federation-board |title=Manawatū dairy farmer Andrew Hoggard elected to International Dairy Federation board |first=Sam |last=Kilmister |date=18 December 2020 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |access-date=6 August 2023}}</ref> Hoggard resigned as Federated Farmers president on 8 May 2023, two months before his term of office was due to end.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/business/farming/131984387/andrew-hoggard-steps-down-early-as-federated-farmers-president |title=Andrew Hoggard steps down early as Federated Farmers president |first=Anna |last=Whyte |date=8 May 2023 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |access-date=6 August 2023}}</ref>

In October 2022 Hoggard, as Federated Farmers national president, criticised the [[Sixth Labour Government of New Zealand|Labour Government]]'s plans to tax the emissions produced by farm animals by 2025. Agricultural emissions by farm animals including burping and urination account for about half of New Zealand's emissions. Hoggard claimed that the tax would hurt the farming sector by discouraging farmers from making a living.<ref>{{cite news |title=New Zealand proposes taxing cow burps to reduce emissions |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-63211506 |access-date=14 October 2022 |work=[[BBC News]] |date=11 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221012112205/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-63211506 |archive-date=12 October 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Farmers, environmentalists weigh in on farm-level pricing plan |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/476486/farmers-environmentalists-weigh-in-on-farm-level-pricing-plan |access-date=14 October 2022 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=11 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221012235317/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/476486/farmers-environmentalists-weigh-in-on-farm-level-pricing-plan |archive-date=12 October 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

Hoggard became a member of [[ACT New Zealand]] in 2019. On 9 May 2023, one day after stepping down as president of Federated Farmers, he was named as the ACT candidate in the Rangitīkei electorate for the [[2023 New Zealand general election]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/national/programmes/checkpoint/audio/2018889416/ex-federated-farmers-boss-hoggard-stands-as-act-candidate |title=Ex-Federated Farmers boss Hoggard stands as ACT candidate |date=9 May 2023 |work=[[RNZ News]] |access-date=6 August 2023}}</ref> Hoggard was subsequently ranked fifth on ACT's party list for the election.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2023/07/election-2023-act-party-reveals-its-list-of-candidates-for-general-election.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724123712/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2023/07/election-2023-act-party-reveals-its-list-of-candidates-for-general-election.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=24 July 2023 |title=Election 2023: ACT Party reveals its list of candidates for general election |first=Scott |last=Palmer |date=16 July 2023 |work=[[Newshub]] |access-date=6 August 2023}}</ref>

===First term, 2023–present===
During the 2023 election, Hoggard came third place in the Rangitīkei electorate, which was won by [[New Zealand National Party|National Party]] candidate [[Suze Redmayne]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Rangitīkei - Official Result |url=https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-41.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=25 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123163450/https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-41.html |archive-date=23 November 2023 |date=3 November 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> He was however elected to Parliament on the ACT party list.<ref>{{cite web |title=2023 General Election - Successful Candidates |url=https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/successful-candidates.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=25 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231122030023/https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/successful-candidates.html |archive-date=22 November 2023 |date=3 November 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Following the formation of the [[Sixth National Government of New Zealand|National-led coalition government]], Hoggard became [[Minister for Biosecurity]], [[Minister for Food Safety]], Associate Minister of Agriculture, and Associate [[Minister of the Environment (New Zealand)|Minister of the Environment]] in late November 2023.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cabinet lineup for new government unveiled - who gets what? |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/503156/cabinet-lineup-for-new-government-unveiled-who-gets-what |access-date=15 December 2023 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=24 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231204122806/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/503156/cabinet-lineup-for-new-government-unveiled-who-gets-what |archive-date=4 December 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> In the agriculture portfolio he is responsible for animal welfare, skills and significant natural areas. In the environment portfolio he is responsible for the Jobs for Nature programme, biodiversity, and freshwater regulations for farmers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Delegations to Associate Ministers {{!}} Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (DPMC) |url=https://www.dpmc.govt.nz/our-business-units/cabinet-office/ministers-and-their-portfolios/delegations |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=www.dpmc.govt.nz |language=en}}</ref>

On 14 March 2024 Hoggard, as Associate Environment Minister, announced that the government would suspend the obligation for councils to impose Significant Natural Areas (SNAs) under the previous [[Sixth Labour Government of New Zealand|Sixth Labour Government]]'s National Policy Statement for Indigenous Biodiversity for three years, while the [[Resource Management Act 1991]] is being replaced.  Significant Natural Areas are places in New Zealand where rare or threatened plants or animals are found. Their protection was previously required under the Resource Management Act.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-03-14 |title=Government drops need for councils to comply with Significant Natural Areas provisions |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/511689/government-drops-need-for-councils-to-comply-with-significant-natural-areas-provisions |access-date=2024-03-14 |website=[[RNZ]] |language=en-nz}}</ref> On 15 March he released a statement saying his 14 March comment had been misunderstood: "To be clear, there has been no change to statutory and regulatory obligations on councils at this point. If my statement has been read in a way that suggested that the change had already come into effect, this was not the intention". [[University of Otago]] law Professor Andrew Geddis said the statement was "misleading at best, and borderline unlawful at worst. No minister can by mere announcement remove an existing legal obligation imposed by a parliamentary enactment."<ref>{{Cite news |title=Andrew Hoggard walks back environment announcement after experts call it unlawful |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2024/03/associate-environment-minister-andrew-hoggard-backtracks-on-significant-natural-areas-announcement.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240315054313/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2024/03/associate-environment-minister-andrew-hoggard-backtracks-on-significant-natural-areas-announcement.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=15 March 2024 |access-date=2024-03-15 |work=[[Newshub]] |language=en}}</ref>

In August 2024, Hoggard as Minister for Food Safety announced the government was not going to sign up to new [[infant formula]] quality standards developed by [[Food Standards Australia New Zealand]] and would instead develop a separate New Zealand standard over the next five years. The announcement was welcomed by the dairy industry but was criticised by the New Zealand College of Midwives.<ref name="g092">{{cite news |date=5 August 2024 |title=NZ opts out of joint standard on infant formula |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2024/08/05/nz-opts-out-of-joint-standard-on-infant-formula/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811192313/https://www.1news.co.nz/2024/08/05/nz-opts-out-of-joint-standard-on-infant-formula/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |access-date=6 April 2025 |website=1News}}</ref> In April 2025 ''[[Radio New Zealand|RNZ]]'' reported that Hoggard had been heavily lobbied by dairy industry representatives, including his sister.<ref name="b718">{{cite news |last=Bradley |first=Anusha |date=3 April 2025 |title=How multinational dairy companies convinced ministers to back away from new rules for baby formula |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/556997/how-multinational-dairy-companies-convinced-ministers-to-back-away-from-new-rules-for-baby-formula |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250406220412/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/556997/how-multinational-dairy-companies-convinced-ministers-to-back-away-from-new-rules-for-baby-formula |archive-date=6 April 2025 |access-date=6 April 2025 |website=RNZ}}</ref> Soon after, ''RNZ'' reported that the government was considering signing up to the standards, following a change of position by the dairy lobbyists.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bradley |first=Anusha |date=7 April 2025 |title=Government considers u-turn on baby formula rules after industry shift |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/in-depth/557379/government-considers-u-turn-on-baby-formula-rules-after-industry-shift |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250406220637/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/in-depth/557379/government-considers-u-turn-on-baby-formula-rules-after-industry-shift |archive-date=6 April 2025 |access-date=7 April 2025 |work=RNZ}}</ref>

In early December 2024, Hoggard as Biosecurity Minister halted all New Zealand poultry exports following an outbreak of the H7N6 subtype of [[avian influenza]] at a [[Moeraki]] farm.<ref>{{cite news |title=All poultry exports on hold until NZ free of highly pathogenic bird flu |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/country/535456/all-poultry-exports-on-hold-until-nz-free-of-highly-pathogenic-bird-flu |access-date=2 December 2024 |work=[[RNZ]] |date=2 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241202103217/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/country/535456/all-poultry-exports-on-hold-until-nz-free-of-highly-pathogenic-bird-flu |archive-date=2 December 2024}}</ref>

In October 2025, Hoggard announced a rewrite of pig welfare laws, cancelling the previous government's plans to ban farrowing crates in favor of a legislative amendment that retained them with stricter regulations and a 10-year transition period. Released documents subsequently revealed that the National Animal Welfare Advisory Committee (NAWAC), the government's independent expert body, had disagreed with the reforms, advising that the continued confinement of sows likely did not meet the standards of the Animal Welfare Act.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Bradley |first=Anusha |date=17 October 2025|title=Govt's independent animal welfare experts disagreed with pig welfare reforms |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/in-depth/576140/govt-s-independent-animal-welfare-experts-disagreed-with-pig-welfare-reforms |access-date=28 January 2026|work=[[RNZ]] |language=en-nz}}</ref>

On 10 March 2026, Hoggard as Associate Agricultural Minister confirmed that the Government would not progress with an ACT and National pledge to reverse the previous government's ban on live animal exports during the [[54th New Zealand Parliament]]ary term, stating that he had been unable to secure consensus within the [[New Zealand Cabinet]]. He said that the Government would instead focus on implementing its reforms to the [[Resource Management Act 1991]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Collins |first1=Benedict |title='Will be disappointment': Live export ban won't be overturned this term |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/03/10/will-be-disappointment-live-export-ban-wont-be-overturned-this-term/ |access-date=10 March 2026 |work=[[1News]] |date=10 March 2026 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20260310204325/https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/03/10/will-be-disappointment-live-export-ban-wont-be-overturned-this-term/ |archive-date=10 March 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 11 May 2026, Hoggard confirmed that the Government would support the creation of investor-funded voluntary carbon and nature projects.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Newton |first1=Kate |title=Voluntary carbon and nature markets bodies endorsed by NZ govt |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/top/594861/voluntary-carbon-and-nature-markets-bodies-endorsed-by-nz-govt |access-date=12 May 2026 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=11 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260512033528/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/top/594861/voluntary-carbon-and-nature-markets-bodies-endorsed-by-nz-govt|archive-date=12 May 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> In 12 May, Hoggard expressed support for an "open seat rule" to allow school children to use rural school buses in order to boost rural school attendance.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Daniel |first1=Mark |title=ACT Proposes ‘Open Seat Rule’ for Rural School Buses |url=https://www.ruralnewsgroup.co.nz/dairy-news/dairy-general-news/act-rural-school-bus-open-seat-rule |publisher=Rural News Group |access-date=12 May 2026 |date=12 May 2026}}</ref>
